plan.summary: Only the team owner will be able to remove people from a team. Admins keep their other powers, such as renaming the team and changing roles, but they will no longer be able to remove members and will not see the remove option.
acceptance_criteria: The team owner can remove a member or an admin from the team.
An admin who tries to remove a member is refused (403) and the member stays in the team.
An ordinary member who tries to remove someone is still refused (403).
On the team settings page the remove option is shown only to the team owner; admins and members do not see it.
Admins can still rename the team and change members' roles.
The team owner cannot be removed from their own team, and a personal team's owner is never removed.
assumptions: "Team owner" means the user with the owner role on that team (the person who created it), as described in the project notes.
The check is enforced on the server through the existing TeamPolicy / form request, not only by hiding the button.
Whether a member can leave a team on their own is not covered by this request; any existing self-leave behaviour is left unchanged.
No database change is needed; roles stay as they are.
plan.current_behavior: Both the team owner and team admins can remove members from a team on the team settings page. Ordinary members cannot remove anyone.
preserve: Admins can still change members' roles.
Admins can still rename the team.
The team owner can still remove members and admins.
The team owner cannot be removed from their own team.
Ordinary members still cannot remove anyone.
Everyone keeps their personal team and can still switch between their teams.
Members can still see the team they belong to.

review.summary: The change removes the 'remove members' permission from the admin role in the single place where role permissions are set, so only the team owner (who holds every permission) can remove people. Admins keep the rename and change-role permissions. New tests check that the owner can remove members and admins, that admins are refused (403) when they try to remove a member, another admin or the owner, and that the owner cannot remove themselves. A settings-page test checks that admins can still manage the team but are not offered the remove option. The project notes were updated to match. Every verification check passed: tests, static analysis, formatting, lint and TypeScript. No tests were deleted. The one changed assertion (an admin trying to remove the owner now gets 403 instead of a validation error) follows directly from the plan. Nothing listed under 'Must stay as it is' was changed.

changes.behavior: Admins removing people from a team
changes.before: An admin could remove members and other admins from the team.
changes.now: Admins can no longer remove anyone. If they try, they are refused and the person stays in the team. Only the team owner can remove members and admins.

changes.behavior: Remove option on the team settings page
changes.before: Both the owner and admins saw the option to remove people from the team.
changes.now: Only the team owner sees the remove option. Admins and ordinary members do not.

changes.behavior: An admin trying to remove the team owner
changes.before: The admin got an error message saying the owner cannot be removed.
changes.now: The admin is refused outright because they are not allowed to remove anyone. The owner still stays in the team.

The team owner can still remove members and admins.

data.account:
Only the team owner can now remove people from a team. The permission is set in one place, config/teams.php, and I removed 'members:remove' from the admin role there. The owner still has every permission through '*'. Everything else already reads that setting: TeamPolicy::removeMember, which TeamMemberDestroyRequest::authorize() uses, so an admin's DELETE now gets a 403 before RemoveTeamMember runs. TeamController's can.removeMembers flag also reads it, and Team.vue already uses that flag to show the remove button, so admins no longer see it. I made no PHP or Vue code changes. Admins keep 'team:update' and 'members:update-role'. RemoveTeamMember's owner guard is unchanged.

Tests: RemoveTeamMemberTest now covers the owner removing an admin (new), an admin refused with 403 when removing a member or another admin (member stays in the team), an admin refused with 403 when removing the owner, and the owner trying to remove themselves getting the 'member' validation error. The 'members cannot remove' test was kept. TeamSettingsTest gains a test that an admin gets updateTeam and updateMemberRoles true but removeMembers false. TeamRoleTest's config-override test now uses 'members:update-role', and a new test checks that only the owner has 'members:remove'. The notes in .builder/project.md and .builder/capabilities/membership.md are updated.

Checks: pint --test passed, phpstan passed with 0 errors, php artisan test passed (71 tests, 260 assertions), npm run types:check (vue-tsc) passed and npm run check (vp format and lint) passed. README.md has no Checks section in this workspace, so I ran the checks found in composer.json and package.json. I did not run fixtures/reference-solutions/verify.sh because that path is not in this workspace and the fixture was not touched.

findings.summary: The verification header says 'unverified' even though every step passed. That is because no protected acceptance tests apply to this change, not because anything failed. It is worth knowing that there was no independent acceptance-test coverage.

No front-end file changed. Hiding the remove option from admins relies on the page reading the 'can.removeMembers' flag. The test checks that this flag is false for admins but not how the page is rendered. That looks fine if the existing page already uses the flag, but it is not checked directly.

No test checks that an ordinary member's settings page reports 'can.removeMembers' as false, or that the owner's page reports it as true. The owner case may already be covered by the existing 'owners can manage the team' test.
